questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good academic performance and opportunities, surrounding nature, great communities for exchange students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Relatively easy, the university provided a lot of good advice. 
The only thing was housing - a bit difficult to find when you're in another country. I didn't get housing on campus, so had to go search myself. Would have been nice to have had a contact overhere that might have been able to check out places (that they weren't scams) before paying a deposit/rent from overseas.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Welcome day on UBC, buddy group/student on campus that I could contact.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. Very expensive and hard to determine scam risks etc. Lots of different messages on different online platforms and forums. But it's not impossible and we definately found a good place in the end, and I was actually very happy living off campus!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Buses connect the city well, so it's not as bad as it could be. However be aware of people charging too much in deposit/the first rent, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy to take and drop courses at UBC. I had good communication with them, and they responded to all of my questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Office hours with professors or GoGlobal. 
Buddy program (student advice) 
Online ressources and communication

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very - i got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out as many courses as you like - use the two weeks of free add/drop period when you get here. Dont stress too much, changes can be made conteniously.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took 300-coruses (year 3 courses). They varied a lot in structure and difficulty.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different from course to course. Generally, I had less hours at UBC on campus than I normally have at UCPH. The classes over here where bigger, and some of them only lectures (as opposed to a lot of group work, which I am used to having at UCPH). One of my classes had a lot of group work, which was nice. Then it is also easier to meet and get to know your fellow students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fertility, Families and Migration
International Agricultural Development
Introduction to Wine Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Fertility, Families and Migration - very interesting subjects and nice structure. No final exam but based on weekly tests and assignments. 
International Agricultural Development - much focus on group work, which is great for meeting other fellow students. Very engaged and flexible professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food and housing was a bit more expensive than I thought. 
And then the madatory Upass (which is actually great and not very expensive when you consider it covers all public transportation while you're here) and the UBC health insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food was more expensive than anticipated. 
But go to Sunrise market if downtown, produce is a bit cheaper there. Otherwice, look into "Sprouts" on campus - they provide community dinners/Fridges if your food budget is struggling.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UBC has more than 100 clubs, and other activities as well. Lots of sports but also e.g. exchange club and other social initiatives. No excuse not to get involved.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a number of activites, but would generally just recommend to get involved in the campus clubs! A good way to meet people and also provides a lot of opportunity to see the area, city and explore different opportunities!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I went swimming once a week with the triathlon club, which I found great! Even if you don't join a swimming team, go to the aquatic centre - it is free for students and very well equipped! 
Also, Join the VOC outdoor club. There you can rent gear and meet like-minded people to go on trips in the weekends and such. We used that club a lot, as do a lot of other exchange students. 
I joined the campus "Agronomy Garden" as I have an interest in making things grow. Further I joined a weekly fitness class in Muay Thai, to challenge myself and learn a new skill.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - The Canadians are very openminded and friendly, so I had no truble on that front.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get involved in the clubs and social life on campus! Some courses only have 1-hour lecrures, where you don't necessarily get to talk to a lot of people. Finding other channels to socialize it a good idea.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Canadians' friendliness and spirit for the outdoors! They don't mind that you're only here for half a year, they'll still want to make friends, and they're easy to talk to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go on trips and explore the outdoors in your free time - don't worry too much about missing school time or being a bit behind in your classes. Take advantage that you only need to pass. 
I learned a lot of new skills and improved some existing ones - e.g. long hikes, skiing, snowshoeing, rock climbing and more. 
Also, I lived with 4 other fantastic roommates and really enjoyed the social part of the exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It is easy to book cars through companies like Turo or Evo, especially if you find a few people to with. Then Gas is not too expensive, and you can go a lot of places in the mountains and do hikes, etc. 
Don't panic too much if you dont get housing on campus - it can be difficult, but everyone I went with and met had been able to find something they liked and somewhere affordable. I ended up enjoying staying off-campus a lot and wouldn't switch now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The community and friends that I've made - a lot of them I'll be able to see back home as well. 
Going on trips and seeing the amazing nature here is defininately also the thing to do here. Some of it is more expensive than others, but make sure you save up a little bit so your budget is not limiting you to do these opportunities!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing on my own - again it was difficult but not impossible, and ended up really appreciating it!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to UBC, it's really the best exchange I can imagine!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
